title: Scale Git evidence validation on growing history
outcome: The workflow validator remains resource-bounded and reaches the intended scope and mutation decisions as unrelated repository history grows, while exact evidence enumeration and every existing workflow-integrity failure remain strict and the complete workflow suite is green at 100% validator coverage.
scope: Use bounded, no-output Git predicates scoped to the exact relevant revision relation and path set for boolean ready-scope and post-integration packet-mutation decisions instead of globally enumerating every changed path.

Keep exact RED/candidate evidence path enumeration capped and preserve strict diagnostics for oversized relevant evidence, streamed Git-output truncation, dirty metadata, ancestry or content mismatches, accepted-phase policy, rename or copy boundaries, and later integrated packet mutation.

Add one dedicated deterministic real-Git regression file whose corruption case creates a syntactically valid bogus commit naming a proven-absent root tree, proves the intrinsic missing relation and exact scoped diff error before validation, and covers 101 unrelated paths, 101 relevant evidence paths, fewer than 100 records producing more than 10,000 streamed bytes, ticket-to-outside renames, and ordinary later ticket mutation.

Restore the complete workflow test task to an exact zero-failure result on the growing current history and retain exact 100% branch, function, and line coverage for ticket_contract.ts and validate_ticket.ts.
nonGoals: Change tools/workflows/ticket_contract.ts, deno.json, task definitions, coverage thresholds, or test discovery semantics.

Copy, merge, cherry-pick, rebase, or otherwise inherit commits, packet state, results, reviews, run IDs, or evidence from blocked WORKFLOW-001; its candidate diff may be consulted only as historical design input after the fresh RED is frozen.
Change any prior ticket packet, application, product, architecture, schema, .agents, .codex, or .git content, or any global, user, or system Git configuration.
Merge or integrate main, create integration.md, push, deploy, or claim broader application or production readiness.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A ready packet with exactly 101 unrelated changed paths reaches its intended allowed-write validation without a global changed-path output-limit failure, while a ticket-to-outside rename is still rejected as an out-of-scope ready change.
acceptanceCriteria.redProof: deno test --allow-read --allow-write --allow-run=deno,git tools/workflows/scalable_git_evidence_regression_test.ts fails on unchanged production only because the 101-unrelated-path ready fixture receives git_output_limit; its rename control and fixture setup succeed.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Accepted post-candidate and integrated packet histories with exactly 101 unrelated later paths each reach the exact scoped mutation decision, while ordinary later ticket mutation and a ticket-to-outside rename from the integrated packet are detected as later ticket mutation.
acceptanceCriteria.redProof: The same focused command fails on unchanged production only where global later-path enumeration reaches git_output_limit before the intended relation/path decision; the integrated rename control remains strict.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Exact evidence enumeration remains capped: exactly 101 relevant RED or candidate paths is rejected, and fewer than 100 records whose actual streamed Git output exceeds 10,000 bytes maps to git_output_limit without weakening evidence comparisons.
acceptanceCriteria.redProof: The same focused command contains passing unchanged-main controls that create real repositories with 101 relevant evidence paths and with fewer than 100 long records exceeding the byte budget, and asserts the existing strict git_output_limit diagnostics.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Broken Git relation evidence maps deterministically to the existing Git-error diagnostic using a syntactically valid commit whose root tree names a proven-absent OID; the fixture never deletes an object file and proves the scoped Git predicate exits greater than 1 before invoking validation.
acceptanceCriteria.redProof: The same focused command contains a passing unchanged-main control that derives an absent OID with git hash-object --stdin without -w, proves cat-file -e fails, creates the bogus commit with git hash-object -t commit -w --stdin --literally, builds valid metadata HEAD with commit-tree and update-ref, proves the bogus commit exists while its root tree remains absent, and proves the exact scoped git diff --quiet relation exits greater than 1 before asserting validator error mapping.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Dirty metadata, ancestry and content mismatches, accepted-phase policy, rename and copy boundaries, later integrated packet mutation, and exact workflow task discovery remain strict; the candidate records the exact workflow test count with zero failures and 100% branch, function, and line coverage for both validator production files.
acceptanceCriteria.redProof: The focused regression preserves explicit controls for each named boundary, while deno task test:workflow remains the independently reproduced baseline failure caused by the global MAX_CHANGED_PATHS cap until the bounded-query implementation is added.

risks: Treating Git diff exit 1 as an execution error, or an exit greater than 1 as a boolean difference, could accept invalid metadata or hide repository corruption.
A broad pathspec or relation could miss rename and copy boundaries, allow out-of-scope ready changes, or fail to detect later mutation of an integrated packet.
Removing caps from exact RED or candidate evidence enumeration could reintroduce unbounded memory and output use under adversarial history.

A fixture that deletes a loose object is vulnerable to packing, alternates, or concurrent maintenance; the missing root-tree relation must be intrinsic to the deliberately bogus commit and explicitly proven before validator use.
Changing task discovery, coverage scope, contracts, or earlier packet metadata would conceal rather than fix the current scalability defect.
